reason: The cited evidence (E1) confirms that rapid quenching produces an amorphous structure, but it provides no data on residual defects, structural relaxation, or the effect of sub-Tg annealing on crystallization behavior. The key premises about defect relaxation, increased nucleation barrier, and delayed crystallization are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Rapid quenching yields a largely amorphous structure with residual defects that can serve as nucleation sites
A sub-Tg isothermal hold allows relaxation of excess free volume and structural defects into a lower-energy, more homogeneous configuration
This relaxation increases the nucleation barrier for crystallization during subsequent heating
